# SPD-023 — transcript_usage counts each request once per content block, so token figures run four to five times too high

## Brief
Claude Code writes an assistant response as one JSONL entry per content block, and every entry repeats that request's message.id and usage. transcript_usage adds usage for every assistant entry, so each request's input and cache tokens are counted once per block, and tool-heavy turns have many blocks. total_tokens, the Team card's Tokens cell and tokens_out/tokens_in/tokens_cached on member notes are all inflated about five times, and SPD-013's token accounting would build on them; SPD-021 makes foreground rows read the same sum. Fix: count each message.id once, taking its last entry's usage (only output_tokens differs between a request's entries, and the last is the final count); messages then counts requests. The four live rows need a decision: re-sum where the transcript still exists (Vitelotte's does; Pompadour's and Cascade's recorded paths are gone) or leave them as they are.

Evidence: Read-only over real subagent transcripts, 2026-09-13. Vitelotte (SPD-010, projects/-Users-ericlugo-Personal-Spud/10791bce-.../subagents/agent-a68336978fb3147ed.jsonl): 134 assistant entries, every one with exactly 1 content block, 25 distinct message ids = 25 distinct requestIds; summed per entry 43,396,713 tokens, last entry per message id 8,927,864; the stored total_tokens is 42,831,980. Chieftain's own transcript mid-run: 48 entries, 8 message ids, 7,208,617 per entry vs 1,243,270 per id. Within one id only output_tokens differs, and the last entry is the maximum on every key (23 of 23 ids in Vitelotte's, 8 of 8 in Chieftain's), e.g. msg_011Cezq1QMQQwog9SjEAaEwe: (input 2, output 5, cache creation 75049, cache read 0) then (2, 234, 75049, 0). Code: bin/spud transcript_usage (messages += 1 and totals += usage for every entry with type assistant).

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus, the persona tier, no children. A data repair would take fable (expensive if wrong), but Eric ruled Fable out again (2026-09-13), so the repair is built to be checked instead: a dry-run-first CLI command that keeps every old figure in an event, run against the live ledger by Spud only after Eric merges, dry run read first. No reviewer and no headless probe; Spud reads the diff and reruns the suite at return. Design decided at start: a transcript sum counts each API request once, by its last entry, and tool uses count distinct blocks; a new sum is marked so an old one can be found; `spud member resum` re-sums old rows from their transcripts, found at the recorded path or, where a worktree session's exit moved the file, by session and file name under the projects directory. All five live rows can be repaired: every transcript was found by agent id, though four recorded paths are stale. The four stale lines of `docs/design/2026-09-12-team-card.md` left by [[SPD-021]] go to the writer at this ticket's merge, with this ticket's own prose, so the doc is edited once.

## Outcome
Merged into main on 2026-09-13 at Eric's word (merge 0156590); Ran 294 tests in 144.614s, OK, no bytecode left, on main after the merge. A transcript sum now counts each API request once, by its last entry, and each tool call once, and is marked "counting": "request". After a dry run, Spud ran `spud --as spud member resum --all` on the live ledger: six members re-summed from their transcripts (one at its recorded path, five moved), tool uses unchanged, durations up by under 14 s where a transcript ran past the recorded stop, and the old figures kept in member.edited events. Tokens before and after: Vitelotte 42,831,980 to 8,927,864; Cascade 80,652,270 to 24,361,555; Pompadour (SPD-015) 47,394,682 to 12,705,420; Sarpo 24,944,470 to 6,020,010; Chieftain 32,173,475 to 8,288,324; and Pompadour (SPD-023) 55,065,306 to 11,753,368, whose own stop was recorded by the code from before the merge.
